text: MCP tools. A defk function can become a tool that an agent calls.
The agent's call runs as a doeff program, and its effects travel out to your handlers.
So a tool reaches the same handlers as the rest of your program.
def-MCP-tool wraps an existing defk in a tool: a name, a description, and typed parameters.
It expands to an MCP tool def. The agent sees the tool's name, and reads its parameters as a JSON schema.
Its handler is an at-do function. Run it, and the defk runs: accepted, buy 100 of 7203.
A program asks for an agent by yielding Launch, with the tools the agent may call.
claude agent handler catches Launch. It captures the handlers around the Launch, and starts an MCP server.
It writes dot MCP dot JSON, starts Claude Code in a terminal, and types the prompt.
Then it resumes k with a session handle.
In this run, the terminal is a fake one, and a script plays the agent's part.
The agent reads dot MCP dot JSON, connects over SSE, and lists the tools.
It calls query price tool. The tool's program yields Quote Price, and paper broker answers: 2480.
A call that breaks the schema never reaches the program. Side hold is refused, and the agent gets the reason.
With side buy, the call goes through. Place Order reaches paper broker, and the order is filled.
Every tool call ran in the program's own VM, under the handlers captured at Launch.
After Stop, the program asks paper broker for its position: 100, the shares the agent bought.
The capture takes the handlers on both sides of the agent handler, so either order gives 100.
MCP tools: your defk becomes the agent's tool, and your handlers decide what its effects mean.
